sentences: Late at night, at the corner of a wall, a young scholar holding a lantern faces a woman whose cloak is drawn over her head.
His feet already point onward; she hangs back half a step, undecided.
Above them the artist wrote a line of verse: the moon is dim, the night is deep, and only these two know their hearts.
Shin Yun-bok never explains; he lets empty space and glances carry the story.
Curiously, the moon here bulges upward, and one astronomer has read it as a partial lunar eclipse and even proposed the date the scene was painted.
It may be the only love scene in Korean art to become a subject of astronomy.
